media:group.media:title: The NTU alumnus coaching Singapore’s national football team | Beyond the Expected
media:group.media:description:
As a boy, Gavin Lee dreamt of playing for Singapore’s national football team. He never imagined he would one day be coaching it.
Today, Gavin is head coach of Singapore’s men’s national football team. A graduate of the National Institute of Education (@NIESingapore), he coached full time while pursuing his degree in sport science and management at #NTUsg.
How did his journey take him from student to national team head coach? Watch Gavin share his story.

entry.title: New smart sensor developed by #NTUsg scientists makes structural stress visible to the naked eye

media:group.media:title: New smart sensor developed by #NTUsg scientists makes structural stress visible to the naked eye
media:group.media:description:
Colour-changing sensor by #NTUsg scientists could make structural stress visible
What if bridges, buildings and other structures could show when they are under stress?
#NTUsg researchers have developed a colour-changing polymer sensor that makes structural stress visible to the naked eye. As stress increases, the material changes colour, helping engineers see where stress is concentrated and how severely it is developing.
The technology could offer a simpler way to monitor bridges, buildings and other infrastructure, while reducing reliance on extensive networks of sensors, wiring and batteries.
https://ntu.sg/COLOUR-CHANGING-SENSOR
#NTUsgResearch #NTUsgInnovation #SmartMaterials @cee-ntusg @NTUCollegeofEngineering

entry.title: #NTUsg's 14th satellite is now in orbit in space

media:group.media:title: #NTUsg's 14th satellite is now in orbit in space
media:group.media:description:
✨ Up, up and away! #NTUsg’s 14th #satellite, 🛰️ CRIMSON-1, has been successfully launched into space. Led by the NTU Satellite Research Centre at the @NTUsgEEE, the mission will test Singapore-developed technologies in orbit.
Next-generation perovskite solar cells will be assessed for their durability and power generation capabilities in the harsh environment of space. On board, edge AI computing will also be used to analyse satellite images directly in space, potentially reducing the amount of raw data that needs to be sent back to Earth.
CRIMSON-1 was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on the Transporter-18 mission and deployed using Exolaunch’s EXOpod Nova system, with support from the National Space Agency of Singapore under the Space Access Programme. https://ntu.sg/NTUSG-CRIMSON-1
#AIatNTUsg #NTUsgResearch #NTUsgInnovation #SpaceTech

entry.title: The NTU alumnus turned Singapore's 'Spice Man' | Beyond the Unexpected

media:group.media:title: The NTU alumnus turned Singapore's 'Spice Man' | Beyond the Unexpected
media:group.media:description:
Jeya was an introvert when he graduated from the #NTUsg Wee Kim Wee School of Communication and Information, with no plans to run a spice shop.
Today he's known across Singapore as the Spice Man, the third-generation owner of Jeya Spices, where he mixes fresh spice blends on the spot.
After his posts and videos went viral in 2020, Jeya began using his online platform to introduce a new generation to the heritage of Singapore's wet markets and the art of spice mixing. He is a familiar face at the wet market and online, where he combines his expertise in spices with his engaging videos and posts – skills he picked up from his years in the trade and from his communications education at #NTUsg.
Watch his journey from NTU alumnus to Singapore's Spice Man.

entry.title: Would you try this umami-flavoured fermented soybean product?

media:group.media:title: Would you try this umami-flavoured fermented soybean product?
media:group.media:description:
MSG is commonly known for adding an umami boost to food, but what if there was an ingredient that could deliver a rich taste alongside high protein content?
Scientists at #NTUsg developed a potential food ingredient by fermenting okara, a nutrient-rich soybean by-product from tofu and soymilk production. The researchers fermented okara with oyster mushroom mycelium, which is the fine, root-like network of a fungus. The process made okara taste better and increased its protein content to between 27.7 and 30.2 per cent by dry weight.
These findings point to a potential way to turn okara, an underutilised food by-product, into a more nutritious and flavourful ingredient, supporting #sustainable #FoodProduction.
https://ntu.sg/Mushroom-Fermentation-Method
#NTUsgResearch #Sustainability #FoodScience

media:group.media:title: First place with zero drivers 🏎🏁
media:group.media:description:
Team Kinetiz, a joint team comprising #NTUsg, UAE technology company K2 and autonomous systems specialist Alp Autonomy, won the world’s first multi-car autonomous race held in Europe
The team won the first place at Italy’s Imola Circuit, finishing ahead of a formidable field of competitors including TUM, PoliMOVE, Constructor and UNIMORE.
This was A2RL's first international race and its first multi-car competition outside Abu Dhabi. Without a driver present, teams had to develop software that can control the car and make split-second decisions on accelerating, braking and steering, while responding to other cars on the track in real time.
Congratulations to Team Kinetiz on their win 🏆
Read more about their achievement here: https://ntu.sg/A2RL-26
📹: K2

entry.title: Singapore's first full-sized electric aircraft takes flight

media:group.media:title: Singapore's first full-sized electric aircraft takes flight
media:group.media:description:
A team from #NTUsg performing flight tests in Germany has flown Singapore's first electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for the first time – a historic milestone in the history of Singapore aviation.
The month-long flight-test campaign, performed in collaboration with experts from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), was the culmination of three years of research. Working with local and international partners, the team developed technology demonstrator aircrafts that were fully designed, engineered and built in Singapore.
In Germany, an 8-metre wingspan aircraft flew to heights above 90 metres while the 3-metre wingspan variant reached speeds of more than 120 km/h, with both aircrafts demonstrating the ability to hover, fly using its fixed wings, as well as transition between the two modes.
The invaluable flight data collected during the tests will be used to further develop technologies and build a base of knowledge and engineering expertise, advancing Singapore's aviation development capabilities.

entry.title: Check out this rare piano at #NTUsg

media:group.media:title: Check out this rare piano at #NTUsg
media:group.media:description:
This SG50 Limited Edition Red Steinway Grand Piano was played by Lang Lang at the 2015 National Day Parade. It is now the centrepiece of the Education Wing Atrium at the newly reopened Nanyang Executive Centre (NEC). 🎹
Prof Louis Phee, Vice President (Innovation and Entrepreneurship), played his renditions of The Moon Represents My Heart and Home as part of the inaugural performance on the NTU campus, reflecting NEC's role in fostering art and culture among the #OneNTU community.
The piano will be played during educational programmes, performances, rehearsals and community engagement activities, ensuring that this piece of Singapore's musical history continues to create wonderful music and inspire future generations. 🎶
Learn more about it here: https://ntu.sg/NEC-Reopening
